title: Weak approximation of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the quasicategories, equivalence edges, coherent functors, full subcategories and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ between small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, with $O$ ordinary. Inert edges are cocartesian edges over opposites of inclusions of consecutive subintervals in $\Delta$; active edges lie over maps whose opposite preserves both endpoints. A categorical fibration means an inner fibration, in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], such that for every $m\in M$ and equivalence edge $u:f(m)\to o$ there is an equivalence edge $\widetilde u:m\to\widetilde o$ in $M$ with $f(\widetilde u)=u$.

Use the ordered joins and coherent join coslices of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], and their opposite slice convention. Explicitly, for a quasicategory $Q$ and vertex $q$, $(Q_{/q})_n$ consists of maps $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to Q$ whose final vertex is $q$, and $(Q_{q/})_n$ consists of maps $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to Q$ whose initial vertex is $q$. Operators act by precomposition on the $\Delta^n$ block, and the projections to $Q$ restrict to that block.

For an object $C\in M$ and any arrow $\alpha:X\to f(C)$ in $O$, view $\alpha$ as a vertex of $B=O_{/f(C)}$. Define the simplicial set representing the coherent factorization infinity category by the degreewise pullback
$$\mathcal H_f(C,\alpha)=M_{/C}\times_{B} B_{\alpha/},$$
where the first map is induced by $f$ and the second is the target projection of the coslice. Thus an $n$-simplex is a pair of maps $s:\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to M$ and $t:\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to O$, with $s$ equal to $C$ at its final vertex, $t$ equal to $f\circ s$ on its final $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0$ block, and $t$ equal to $\alpha$ on the edge joining its first and last vertices. For $\theta:[r]\to[n]$, the operator is precomposition by $\Delta(\theta)\star\mathrm{id}$ on $s$ and by $\mathrm{id}\star\Delta(\theta)\star\mathrm{id}$ on $t$.

Let $\mathcal F_f(C,\alpha)$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal H_f(C,\alpha)$ on those vertices for which the first edge $\gamma:X\to f(D)$ of the corresponding triangle $X\to f(D)\to f(C)$ is inert in $O$. In particular, an object is $\beta:D\to C$, an inert $\gamma:X\to f(D)$, and a $2$-simplex witnessing $f(\beta)\gamma\simeq\alpha$. Morphisms retain the triangles $\beta'h\simeq\beta$ and $f(h)\gamma\simeq\gamma'$ and their compatibility; the displayed simplicial model specifies all higher coherences. Inertness is imposed on $\gamma$, not on the comparison edge $h$.

When $f$ is a categorical fibration, it is a weak approximation if $\mathcal F_f(C,\alpha)$ is weakly contractible for every $C$ and every $\alpha$. Weakly contractible here means that the unique map of its underlying simplicial set to $\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, with realization and homotopy groups as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A general $f$ is a weak approximation if there exist a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad $M'$, an equivalence $e:M\to M'$ of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, and a categorical fibration $g:M'\to O$ of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, all over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, such that $f=g\circ e$ and $g$ is a weak approximation by the preceding definition. This is a predicate asserting the existence of such a factorization; it does not choose a replacement.

A fibration of generalized nonsymmetric operads is an inert-preserving categorical fibration; no cocartesian-fibration condition on f or its replacement is imposed. Reused the existing infinity-operad, horn-fibration, coherent-join and weak-contractibility notions; specified the coherent factorization category by its degreewise slice/coslice pullback and simplicial operators, and stated the arbitrary-map predicate through an existential strict factorization. This is a definition, with no proof steps or new nodes. Independent Mathlib and project-source searches found no exact attachment or Mathlib definition.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N2-1c3cc60d8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the definition in full against the source, Gepner–Haugseng arXiv:1312.3178v4. The PDF was fetched and converted to text; it is not in literature/. Def. 3.1.19 says a fibration of generalized operads is an inert-preserving categorical fibration, and cocartesian fibration is a separate notion, so the repair that removes the cocartesian requirement is correct. The definition matches Def. A.6.1 clause by clause: M generalized, O ordinary; for every C and every arbitrary α, the full subcategory of M_{/C} ×_{O_{/f(C)}} (O_{/f(C)})_{α/} on pairs with γ inert is weakly contractible; inertness is imposed on γ only, not on the comparison edge h. The general-map clause is the factorization f = g∘e with e an equivalence and g a categorical fibration that is a weak approximation, and it is purely existential. The slice and coslice simplices and operators are correct, and the pullback is a quasicategory by lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration. Weak contractibility includes the component condition, so an empty category does not count. The inner-fibration plus equivalence-lifting form of categorical fibration is Joyal's characterization for quasicategories. All five stmt_deps are used and supply exactly what is taken from them. Small cases checked: f = id (the pair (α, id) is initial even for non-inert α), M empty, nullary and [0] objects. The citers (the active-lift criterion, E.0.2, and the algebra-invariance lemma, A.6.5) are consistent with the definition. No duplicate exists in the DAG or in the main-20261015 blueprint; lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction is the different symmetric notion. There are no new nodes and no proof steps, nothing cites SGA, and nothing was changed. One note, not a fault: the Kan M_[0] convention is inherited from lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability and is stricter than GH Def. 2.4.1.
